title: Bind JetBrains approval to the rendered plan
description: Objective: close PlanReviewDialog's stale-render hole using the landed JetBrains model/wire child task-0ad3744e77bd43b08b9c0b63293912a6. Deliverable: freeze a valid reviewed plan revision only after initial DoD/steps render; on a changed revision latch Approve disabled with a localized 'Plan changed - close and reopen to review' notice rather than partially re-rendering the plan. onState must invalidate before the comments-equality return and before the 200ms comment debounce; missing task, non-AWAITING_APPROVAL status, invalid revision and disconnected service cannot approve. The action must independently recheck getState()/isConnected() against the captured revision, but must never substitute the cache's newer revision. Use a production-used headless presenter/state helper in a new src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalState.kt plus new src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalStateTest.kt; existing files are toolwindow/PlanReviewDialog.kt and src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties (4 files total). Disable repeated sends while approval pending. Keep dialog open on send failure or daemon APPROVE_TASK error, show the existing onError message without treating transport success as approval; only observed authoritative state may finish an approval. EDT-safe callbacks, stopped debounce timers and removed listener on disposal are mandatory. NOT in scope: rewriting all board/detail approval routes, in-place mutation stamping policy, or VS Code. Tests cover new revision with identical comments, same-revision comment update, forced action while disabled, stale/deleted/status-changed task, invalid stamp, send failure/disconnection, error, duplicate click, reopen and disposal. Gate at repo root on Windows: cmd /d /c "cd /d moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test"; Unix: cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test. Reuse the headless JUnit approach, require nonzero counts and red-on-old evidence; serialize shared Gradle outputs.
definitionOfDone: JUnit on the production-used presenter proves the token sent is the successfully rendered revision, never the latest cached one; reopening renders/captures the new revision.

A revision update with unchanged comments invalidates before debounce/early return, shows the refresh notice and prevents even a forced approval action; comment-only same-revision updates stay usable.
Deleted task, changed status, malformed revision or disconnected service cannot send an approval; repeated/pending clicks send at most once, asserted against captured outgoing command.
Send failure or daemon error retains usable failure feedback without reporting approval success; state transitions and disposed callbacks are handled without stale sends or leaked listeners/timers.
Fresh Gradle test exits 0 with nonzero JUnit counts, with scoped red-on-old regression evidence and no unrelated approval entry-point changes.
taskRails: Use disable-and-reopen UX, not partial plan rendering or automatic approval of a newer cached revision.
Never equate transport send success to daemon acceptance.
Consume the centralized steps-plus-DoD revision contract, including in-place mutations; daemon stamping implementation belongs to the producer, not this UI slice.

implementationPlan.description: VERIFY THE PREREQUISITE CONTRACT, THEN EXPLORE. Read-only, no edits, no diff. (a) Prove slice 3 (task-0ad3744e77bd43b08b9c0b63293912a6, 'Carry plan revisions through JetBrains commands') actually landed: `git log --oneline --grep "Moe-Task: task-0ad3744e77bd43b08b9c0b63293912a6"` must find a commit, and `grep -n planRevision moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeCommandSender.kt` must show the field and the widened command. If it has not landed, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ['task-0ad3744e77bd43b08b9c0b63293912a6'] - do NOT implement the model/wire layer here. (b) Write down three facts about the delivered contract, because this plan deliberately does not assume them: how Task carries the revision (a safe Long, and how a legacy missing stamp is represented); whether a MALFORMED stamp is distinguishable from a MISSING one (the parser contract requires it; if slice 3 collapsed them, record that limitation in the step note and follow slice 3's documented behavior rather than inventing a client-side content hash, which the task rails forbid); and the exact signature and return type of MoeProjectService.approveTask now that it carries a revision and a send result. (c) Confirm the revision parameter is OPTIONAL with a default. Four other approval entry points call approveTask(taskId) today - actions/ApproveTaskAction.kt:17, toolwindow/MoeToolWindowPanel.kt:511 and :570, toolwindow/TaskDetailDialog.kt:580 - and this task's Definition of Done forbids touching them. If slice 3 made the parameter required, stop and report rather than widening past four files. (d) Re-read the seams you will edit: PlanReviewDialog.onState (lines 162-197: it assigns `task = updated`, then early-returns on equal comments, then schedules a 200ms debounce), createCenterPanel (54-119, where the Definition of Done and steps panels are actually built), createActions (304-328, where approve currently does `service.approveTask(task.id)` then closes immediately), and dispose (201-207). Note that MoeStateListener already declares `onError(operation, message)` with an empty default body and MoeMessageDispatcher routes daemon ERROR frames to it, so this dialog overrides an existing hook rather than inventing one. Read src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MetricsPanelTest.kt as the headless JUnit pattern to copy, and note the trap recorded in memory gotcha-kotlin-companion-nested-class: a class nested inside a `companion object` is NOT importable as Outer.Inner, so every shared data class goes on the outer class body.

CREATE THE HEADLESS PRESENTER AND ITS MESSAGE KEYS. New file moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalState.kt holding the entire approval decision machine with NO Swing, IntelliJ or service imports - that is what makes it drivable by plain JUnit and what keeps it independent of slice 3's exact API. Declare the data types on the OUTER class body, never inside a companion object. Shape: `class PlanReviewApprovalState(private val taskId: String)` plus `data class TaskSnapshot(val present: Boolean, val status: String?, val revision: RevisionToken)`; a sealed `RevisionToken` with `Present(value: Long)`, `LegacyMissing` and `Malformed`; a sealed `Decision` with `Send(taskId: String, expectedPlanRevision: Long)` and `Blocked(messageKey: String)`; and an enum `Phase { AWAITING_RENDER, READY, PENDING, INVALIDATED, FINISHED, DISPOSED }`. The presenter owns exactly one policy rule about tokens: LegacyMissing is the effective revision 0 and is approvable, Malformed is never approvable. Transitions, every one of them synchronized because onState can arrive off the event dispatch thread while the action reads on it: `onRendered(snapshot)` is called ONLY after the Definition of Done and steps panels rendered without throwing, and captures the revision - a Malformed or absent-task or non-AWAITING_APPROVAL snapshot leaves the presenter blocked with a reason key and never captures. `onStateUpdate(snapshot)` returns whether the UI must change and moves to INVALIDATED when the task vanished, its status left AWAITING_APPROVAL, or its revision differs from the captured one - with the single exception that a PENDING approval observing status WORKING becomes FINISHED, which is the ONLY way an approval completes. `onApproveClicked(connected: Boolean, snapshot: TaskSnapshot)` is the independent action-time recheck: it returns Send ONLY from phase READY with connected true, the task present, the status still AWAITING_APPROVAL and the snapshot revision equal to the CAPTURED one, and the Send always carries the captured revision, never the snapshot's newer value; anything else returns Blocked with a specific key, and a successful Send moves to PENDING so a second click is Blocked. `onSendFailed()` and `onDaemonError(operation, message)` return PENDING to READY so the dialog stays open and usable - neither ever reaches FINISHED, because transport success is not daemon acceptance. `onDisposed()` is terminal and makes every later callback a no-op. Expose read-only `approveEnabled` and `noticeKey` for the dialog to apply. Every Blocked key must be a distinct constant so a test can tell the causes apart. Add the matching keys to moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties in the existing moe.message.* block, including the invalidation notice worded as a close-and-reopen instruction, plus keys for not connected, task missing, status changed, unusable revision, approval already in flight, send failed and daemon error with a parameter for the message. Documented error handling: the presenter never throws for bad input - an unusable snapshot is a Blocked decision, not an exception - because it runs inside Swing callbacks where a throw would leave the dialog wedged.

COVER THE PRESENTER WITH HEADLESS JUNIT. New file moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalStateTest.kt, JUnit 4 in the MetricsPanelTest style: no IntelliJ fixture, no Swing, no daemon. Every test asserts an exact value - a specific Decision subtype, a specific message key constant, a specific captured revision - never a bare truthiness check. Required cases, one per Definition of Done item. Rendered capture: after onRendered with revision 7, a click at revision 7 yields Send with expectedPlanRevision 7; after an update to revision 8 the click never yields Send and never carries 8, which is the core 'token sent is the rendered revision, never the latest cached one' proof. Reopen: a FRESH presenter rendered at revision 8 sends 8, modelling close-and-reopen. Identical comments: an update carrying a NEW revision but unchanged comments still invalidates - this is the case the dialog's old early return swallowed, so it is asserted at the presenter level and again at the dialog level in the next step. Same revision with changed comments leaves the presenter READY and approvable. Forced action while invalidated returns Blocked, proving a caller that ignores the disabled button still cannot send. Deleted task, status moved off AWAITING_APPROVAL, Malformed revision and connected false each return their own distinct Blocked key and no Send. Legacy: LegacyMissing renders and sends effective revision 0. Duplicate clicks: two clicks produce exactly one Send, asserted by collecting every returned Decision into a list and checking the list, which is the captured-outgoing-command assertion the Definition of Done asks for. Transport: onSendFailed returns to READY, a retry sends once more, and the presenter is never FINISHED from a send result alone. Daemon error: onDaemonError while PENDING returns to READY with a usable failure key and no approval. Authoritative finish: only a PENDING presenter observing status WORKING reaches FINISHED. Disposal: after onDisposed every callback is inert and no Send is ever produced, proving no stale send after the dialog closed. Concurrency: drive onStateUpdate and onApproveClicked from two threads against one presenter and assert at most one Send total. Add one guard test that loads /messages/MoeBundle.properties from the test classpath with java.util.Properties and asserts every message key the presenter can emit is actually defined, so a missing localization is a test failure rather than a runtime placeholder. Run `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` (Windows: `cmd /d /c "cd /d moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test"`) and require green with nonzero counts.

WIRE THE DIALOG TO THE PRESENTER. Edit moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewDialog.kt only. (a) Hold a PlanReviewApprovalState built from task.id, and add a notice label to the header area that is hidden until the presenter reports a notice key. (b) Capture after render, not before: at the END of createCenterPanel, once createDodPanel and createStepsPanel have both returned, call onRendered with a snapshot built from the current task; wrap the render in try/catch so a rendering failure logs and leaves the presenter uncaptured and the approve button disabled - failing closed is the required error handling here, since an unrendered plan was never reviewed. (c) In onState, call the presenter FIRST - immediately after `task = updated` and strictly BEFORE the `if (oldComments == newComments) return` early return and before any debounce scheduling - and when it reports a change, apply it in its own SwingUtilities.invokeLater that disables the approve action and shows the notice. That invokeLater must not be inside the debounce timer, or a revision change arriving with identical comments would never reach the screen. Leave the existing comment debounce exactly as it is for same-revision comment updates. (d) Replace the approve action body: build a fresh snapshot from service.getState() at click time, pass it with service.isConnected() to onApproveClicked, and act on the Decision - Send calls the service with the captured revision and then does NOTHING else, no close, because transport success is not approval; Blocked shows the localized message and keeps the dialog open. Disable the approve action while pending so a repeated click cannot send twice even if the button is somehow re-armed. (e) If the delivered service call reports a send result, feed a failure into onSendFailed; override onError(operation, message) to feed onDaemonError, re-enabling the action and showing the existing message unchanged. (f) Close with OK_EXIT_CODE only when the presenter reaches FINISHED, which happens only from observed authoritative state. (g) In dispose, call onDisposed BEFORE stopping the debounce timer and removing the listener, so nothing queued can send after teardown; keep the existing timer stop, pendingUpdate clear and removeListener. Change nothing in createDodPanel, createStepsPanel, renderComments, the reject action or the ask-a-question path, and do not touch the four unrelated approval entry points named in step 1.

RED-ON-OLD EVIDENCE AND THE FULL GATE. The presenter is a new file, so 'fails on the old behaviour' is proven by mutation rather than by running the new test against an empty tree - restore the checkout after each mutation and verify with a separate git status call, never trusting the edit alone. Perform and record at least these four, naming the exact tests that fail for each: move the presenter call in onState to AFTER the comments-equality early return, which must break the new-revision-with-identical-comments case; make onApproveClicked send the snapshot's current revision instead of the captured one, which must break the rendered-token case and is the precise defect this task exists to fix; delete the PENDING guard so a duplicate click sends twice, which must break the at-most-one-Send assertion; and treat a successful send as approval by reaching FINISHED from onSendFailed's sibling path, which must break the transport-is-not-acceptance case. Then run the gate clean from the repo root - Windows `cmd /d /c "cd /d moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test"`, Unix `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` - and require exit 0 with nonzero JUnit counts and no regression in the existing MetricsPanelTest, CreateTaskDialogTest, MoeSettingsDialogTest, MoeJsonTest or the services tests. Gradle output is a shared resource on this box: serialize it through the Moe resource protocol rather than running concurrently with another agent's Gradle build, and do not clean a peer's cache. Keep the exact command, exit code and counts for the verification argument of moe.complete_task, and keep the mutation evidence for QA.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, THEN HAND OFF. Re-read the whole diff as an attacker and confirm each of these or fix it: a revision change with byte-identical comments really reaches the screen and really disables approve, because the old early return is exactly what hid it; the token sent is the captured one on every path and the newer cached revision is never substituted, including after several updates; no path closes the dialog on transport success, and only observed authoritative state finishes an approval; a click while disconnected, on a deleted task, on a task whose status moved, or with an unusable revision produces no outgoing command; two rapid clicks and two concurrent callbacks still send at most once; after dispose nothing can send and no listener or timer is left behind; the presenter cannot throw into a Swing callback; every message key resolves; and the four unrelated approval entry points, the reject path and the ask-a-question path are untouched. Confirm the diff is exactly the four scoped files with nothing from VS Code or Wave 1. State the honest boundary in the completion summary: this binds the JetBrains review dialog to the plan it rendered, and the daemon-side compare-and-swap in sibling task-dd743a02000e46cca6ae2442a1821066 is what actually refuses a stale token - a client that omits the token still takes the legacy path, and automatic SPEED and TURBO approvals are unchanged by design. Then call moe.complete_task with the gate command, exit code, counts and the recorded mutation evidence, listing every modified path in modifiedFiles.

comments.content: Scope clarification received after creation: governor-c9adec43 ruled in msg-2af1526f3f154a76af884f5ddb637293 that planRevision covers all steps+DoD changes, including amend_plan_step and WS UPDATE_TASK. The last task rail only excludes implementing daemon stamping in this UI slice; its 'parent scope decision' wording is now resolved, not a blocker. Use the same rendered-revision model for any such update; no additional client content hash is needed. Producer task-492b573920264188888d56638dd98d81 has the centralized all-writer stamping clarification.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Putting the decision logic directly in PlanReviewDialog and testing it through an IntelliJ fixture - rejected: the existing suite is headless plain JUnit, and a DialogWrapper test needs a platform fixture the build deliberately strips arguments for. (2) Having the presenter depend on the Task model and the service - rejected: slice 3 is not landed yet, so binding the presenter to its types would make this whole slice unbuildable and untestable until that lands; a presenter over plain values keeps slice 3's API confined to a handful of dialog lines. (3) Re-rendering the plan in place when the revision changes - rejected by a task rail: the required UX is latch-disabled plus a close-and-reopen notice, because a partial re-render is exactly how a reviewer ends up approving something they never read. (4) Comparing a client-side hash of the rendered steps and Definition of Done - rejected by the task comment: the daemon's centralized revision already covers in-place mutations, so a second client-side notion of freshness would drift. (5) Closing the dialog on send success - rejected: transport success is not daemon acceptance, so only an observed status move finishes an approval. (6) Returning localized strings from the presenter - rejected: it returns stable message keys so it stays free of IntelliJ imports and the tests can assert exact causes.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The stale-render hole is concrete and visible: onState assigns `task = updated` and then returns early when comments are equal, so a plan whose steps or Definition of Done changed silently replaces the reviewed task object while the screen keeps showing the old plan, and the approve action then sends for whatever task.id holds. The approve action also closes on OK_EXIT_CODE the instant it calls the service, so a send that never left the socket looks exactly like an approval. MoeStateListener.onError already exists as a defaulted interface method routed from real daemon ERROR frames, so daemon-side refusals are observable without touching the service layer. MoeCommandSender.approveTask currently swallows its own ensureConnected result, which is precisely the send-result gap that prerequisite slice 3 owns. There are four other approval entry points (ApproveTaskAction:17, MoeToolWindowPanel:511 and :570, TaskDetailDialog:580) that this task must leave alone, which only works if slice 3 gave the revision parameter a default. Kotlin trap already paid for once in this repo: a class nested inside a companion object is not importable as Outer.Inner, so shared data types go on the outer class body. Main resources are on the test runtime classpath, so a plain JUnit test can load /messages/MoeBundle.properties and assert key coverage without any IntelliJ fixture.
planningNotes.risks: Ordering inside onState is the whole defect: any presenter call placed after the comments-equality return, or any notice applied inside the debounce timer, reintroduces exactly the bug being fixed - assert it behaviorally, and prove it by mutation. The presenter is touched from both the state callback and the event dispatch thread, so every transition must be synchronized or a duplicate send becomes a real race rather than a theoretical one. Never let the click substitute the snapshot's newer revision for the captured one; that is the single most likely wrong implementation because it makes the naive test pass. The revision must stay a safe Long end to end - do not narrow it to Int anywhere. A legacy row with no stamp is approvable as effective 0, but a malformed stamp is never approvable, so those two states must not collapse into one nullable value. If slice 3 made the revision parameter required rather than defaulted, four unrelated approval entry points would stop compiling and the file scope would blow past four - stop and report instead of widening. Gradle output is a shared resource here: serialize it, and do not clean a peer's cache. The bundle keys must exist or the UI shows a raw placeholder at exactly the moment a reviewer needs the warning, which is why a key-coverage test is part of the suite. Do not touch VS Code or Wave 1, and do not claim this slice alone prevents stale approvals - the daemon compare-and-swap in the sibling task is what refuses a stale token.
